# The sharp common-five deletion bound

## Configuration and statement

Use the 120 E8 root lines with doubled integer representatives of squared norm eight, first nonzero coordinate positive. Remove the eight frame lines `2e_0 +/- 2e_1, ..., 2e_6 +/- 2e_7`, and sort the remaining 112 representatives lexicographically. Write them as `r_t`.

Let `c_t` be the integral coordinates of `r_t` in the simple system in the pinned geometry source. Its binary label is

```text
ell(t) = 1 | sum_j ((c_t[j] mod 2) << (j+1)) in F2^9.
```

For a binary seven-space V, write `Lambda(V)={t:ell(t) in V}`. For nonzero `h in K^8`, where K is any characteristic-zero field, write `Off(h)={t:<r_t,h> != 0}`.

**Theorem.** Fix V and one set P of at most five live lines. There are at most two projective directions `[h]` satisfying

```text
rank_F2 {ell(t): t in Off(h) \ (Lambda(V) union P)} <= 7.
```

The bound of two is attained. The deletion allowance five is sharp: at six common deletions, three linearly independent directions can satisfy the condition.

This differs from PR3230's independently chosen five-line cuts. That package disproves the separate-five version; it does not disprove this common-five theorem.

## Reduction to two seven-spaces

A residual label span of dimension at most seven extends to a binary seven-space G. Thus a qualifying direction has

```text
D(V,h,G) = Off(h) \ (Lambda(V) union Lambda(G)) subset P.
```

Conversely, this containment supplies the required residual rank bound. We therefore enumerate exactly the completions G with `|D|<=5`.

A seven-space is the common kernel of two independent binary functionals a,b. Its annihilator has exactly three nonzero elements `a,b,a^b`. Choosing `a<b<a^b` enumerates every annihilator once, giving `(511*510)/6=43,435` seven-spaces. Their live traces have 43,181 distinct masks. Distinct binary spaces with the same live trace are interchangeable for this question.

Eight signed coordinate permutations preserve E8 and its removed frame:

- swap the two coordinates in each of the four frame pairs;
- exchange two adjacent frame pairs;
- change the signs of coordinates zero and two.

The primary and reference implementations verify the root/frame permutations and closure of the complete live-trace set under these generators. They partition the 43,181 traces into 121 orbits. `RESULT.json` retains every representative mask and orbit size. Consequently one first-space representative per orbit suffices, while every second space G is still examined.

The exact two-flat census gives

```text
max_{V,G} |Lambda(V) union Lambda(G)| = 68.
```

The primary implementation checks every G at each first-space representative. The reference independently constructs all annihilators in reduced row-echelon form and recomputes all 121 maxima. Any direction affordable with five cuts therefore has at most 73 off-lines, hence at least 39 live orthogonal root lines.

## Completeness of the direction alphabet

The root-classification step uses the standard real Weyl-chamber theorem for the E8 root system. The pinned geometry checks its integral simple-root coordinates, positive/negative simple-coordinate signs, all 960 simple reflections and the following parabolic counts.

Every real nonzero direction can be moved to the closed fundamental chamber. Its orthogonal roots form the parabolic subsystem generated by the vanishing simple coordinates. Rank at most six permits at most 36 full root lines. This follows by checking all 28 six-generator parabolics; smaller ones extend to these. Thus 39 live zero lines force a rank-seven zero subsystem.

For the eight maximal parabolics, the full root-line counts are

```text
42, 28, 22, 14, 16, 23, 37, 63.
```

Only the first and last can contain 39 live zero lines. Their one-dimensional normals generate projective Weyl orbits of sizes 1,080 and 120. Exact integral reflections reconstruct all 1,200 directions. Their live off-support histogram is

| Off-support size | Directions |
|---:|---:|
| 53 | 112 |
| 56 | 8 |
| 70 | 128 |
| 73 | 896 |
| 76 | 56 |

The 56 directions of support 76 are harmless extra candidates and cannot pass the 68-plus-five budget.

The same completeness statement holds over any characteristic-zero K. For a proposed h, its zero equations have rational coefficients. In their rational nullspace, each declared nonzero equation is a proper rational hyperplane, because h does not annihilate it after scalar extension to K. An infinite rational field is not a finite union of proper linear subspaces. Choose a rational, hence real, vector with exactly the same root zeros. The preceding argument shows that these zeros span rank seven. Their nullspace over K is therefore the scalar extension of one rational line. Thus h itself represents one of the enumerated projective directions. This argument neither orders K nor infers a characteristic-zero identity from a finite-field sample.

## Exhaustive common-cut test

For each of the 121 first-space representatives and every one of the 1,200 directions, the direct C++ census computes every completion G with `|D(V,h,G)|<=5`. Its only early rejection is the necessary inequality

```text
|Off(h)| <= max_G |Lambda(V) union Lambda(G)| + 5.
```

There are 148 qualifying completion records in total. Their distribution by first-space representative is

| Completion records | Representatives |
|---:|---:|
| 0 | 64 |
| 1 | 29 |
| 2 | 22 |
| 9 | 3 |
| 16 | 3 |

The full table is in `RESULT.json`. Each class contains its maximum two-flat union and rows `[direction_index, second_flat_index, decimal_cut_mask]`. Directions are the lexicographically sorted primitive integer representatives of the two Weyl orbits. Second flats are ordered by the canonical functional pair `a<b<a^b`.

Python verifies every emitted cut directly. For every three records with distinct projective directions, their cut union has more than five lines. If three directions worked for one common P, choosing one completion for each would give three such records with union contained in P. This contradiction proves the theorem. There are also 28 compatible distinct-direction record pairs, so the two-direction positive control is nonvacuous.

The reference does not repeat the direct scan. It first finds individual functionals whose violated residual live points number at most five. Any successful pair must use two such functionals. It enumerates their canonical two-planes and tests their violation unions. An independent lattice reconstruction, rational label solver, RREF flat enumeration and this dual-functional search reproduce all 148 records exactly. Both implementations check complete domains, not heuristic samples.

## Literal sharpness witness at six

Take V with annihilator `(60,65)` and one common set

```text
P = {24,34,35,100,101,110}.
```

Use these directions and completions:

| h | G annihilator | D(V,h,G) |
|---|---|---|
| `(0,2,0,-2,0,0,0,0)` | `(62,64)` | `24,35,101,110` |
| `(0,2,0,2,0,0,0,0)` | `(3,124)` | `24,34,35,101,110` |
| `(2,0,-2,0,0,0,0,0)` | `(63,67)` | `24,35,100,101,110` |

Their Gram matrix is `8 I_3`, with determinant 512. They are independent over every characteristic-zero field. All three residual label ranks after deleting the same P are seven. The common set has binary label-span rank four.

For a literal index check, the six deleted lines are

| t | r_t | ell(t) |
|---:|---|---:|
| 24 | `(0,2,-2,0,0,0,0,0)` | 17 |
| 34 | `(0,2,0,2,0,0,0,0)` | 61 |
| 35 | `(0,2,2,0,0,0,0,0)` | 29 |
| 100 | `(2,0,-2,0,0,0,0,0)` | 25 |
| 101 | `(2,0,0,-2,0,0,0,0)` | 57 |
| 110 | `(2,0,0,2,0,0,0,0)` | 53 |

The reference enumerates all five-cut completions for this triple. Their counts are `7,1,1`; their minimum possible common union is six. Thus simply changing its displayed completions cannot produce a common-five witness. Conversely, the union of the first two displayed cuts has five lines and admits those two directions, attaining the theorem's bound.

No claim follows that these directions are normalized relations of independent physical pieces. This is not a new historical TWOSIDE exclusion, a full C5 proof, a decoder-cost floor, a supplier construction or an improved multiplication exponent.
